dials.label: Buy new coins
dials.help: Turn off to stop buying. Coins already held are still watched and sold by the rules below.

choices: Score: the Radar's main 0 to 100 score
DexScreener: how fast the price is moving right now
Quality: how clean the holders look
Blend: the Score and DexScreener averaged
dials.label: Score to buy on
dials.help: The number the bot watches. Score is the Radar's overall rating. DexScreener rates live price movement. Quality rates the holders (top 10, dev, bundlers). Blend averages Score and DexScreener.

dials.label: Buy when the score reaches
dials.help: The bot buys a coin the moment its score is at or above this. Lower means more buys, higher means fewer but stronger ones. Learning can raise it by a few points after a run of losses.

choices: Strict: only the Radar's recommended buys, clean holders, $15k+ liquidity
Normal: any coin that reaches the score, with the usual safety checks
Loose: thinner coins too, only the worst warnings block a buy
dials.label: How picky
dials.help: Safety checks on top of the score. Normal skips coins with Radar warnings, a risky safety rating, more than one failed holder check, under $8k liquidity, under $3k of 5-minute volume, more sells than buys, or a dump in progress. Strict tightens all of these and also needs the Radar's own buy call. Loose relaxes them.

dials.label: SOL per buy
dials.help: How much each buy spends. The bot buys the same coin at most twice a day.

dials.label: Most coins held at once
dials.help: No new buys while this many coins are held.

dials.label: Stop buying for the day after losing
dials.help: Once the account is down this much today, the bot stops buying until tomorrow. 0 turns this off.

dials.label: Wallet Score needed to buy
dials.help: The Wallet Score rates who holds a coin and how much they put in. Holders with a real stake who held coins that went on to grow 3x before they peaked raise it, and so do holders whose own trades in earlier coins made money (total buy-in against total profit, read from the chain); holders whose coins died or who lost money lower it; tiny holders (under $100 or 0.3% of supply) are ignored. 50 means no holder with a real stake has a record yet. Coins under this number are skipped. 0 turns it off.

dials.label: Check DexScreener before buying
dials.help: On: before each buy the bot gets a live DexScreener quote and skips coins whose price, volume or holders look off, and it prices its trades from live quotes. Off: the bot trusts the Radar feed alone (Pulse prices, no DexScreener quote), checks every 2 seconds instead of 5 and buys on the first reading at the score. DexScreener often lags on brand-new coins and blocks some that run: in an overnight test the same Radar 70 bot made about +3% a trade with this off and lost about 10% a trade with it on.

dials.label: Profit target
dials.help: Sell the whole position once the price is this far above what the bot paid.

dials.label: Stay in while momentum is strong
dials.help: At the target the bot reads the chart: price still rising over the last 30 seconds and minute, more buys than sells, the DexScreener score holding up. If most of that is true it keeps holding, and sells as soon as the momentum fades, the price falls back to the target, or it drops the amount below from its high.

dials.label: While staying in, sell this far off the high
dials.help: Only used past the target while the bot rides momentum. It never sells below the target price this way.

dials.label: Stop loss
dials.help: Sell everything once the price is this far below what the bot paid. A sudden jump or drop must hold for about 15 seconds before it counts, so one stale price quote cannot sell a coin. Radar warnings such as liquidity being pulled still sell at once. 0 turns this off.

dials.label: Longest hold
dials.help: Sell after this long, unless the bot is past the target and still riding strong momentum. 0 means no limit.

dials.label: Learn from trades and watched coins
dials.help: The bot keeps notes on every coin near its buy level and on its own trades: how each did afterwards, by score, age, buy share, liquidity and viewers. Setups that keep losing are skipped, and after a run of losing trades the buy level goes up a few points until the bot wins again.

dials.label: Learn the best moment to buy
dials.help: Also learns when to buy: right after a spike or on a dip, how far below its recent high, and the time of day. If coins in that spot usually fall, the bot waits and buys once the coin reaches a spot that usually pays.

dials.label: Learn from bad buys
dials.help: After every trade the bot looks back at the moment it bought: the chart (a spike just before, late in the run, at its high), the volume and liquidity (shrinking, thin, being pulled), the buy share and the holders (Wallet Score, whales), and what the price did afterwards. Each losing trade gets a reason in the activity log. When the same mistake loses at least 5 times out of 7 or so, coins that would repeat it are skipped until it clears.

choices: Auto: follow the network, up to the max fee
Manual: my own priority fee and bribe
dials.label: Network fee
dials.help: Paid in SOL on every buy and every sell, like Axiom's fee settings. A 1% trading fee and 1% slippage each way are always counted too.

choices: Low: the cheapest that usually lands
High: lands first when it is busy
dials.label: Auto fee speed
dials.help: Estimated from live Jito tips and Solana priority fees. Only used with Auto.

dials.label: Max auto fee
dials.help: The most Auto pays per trade, priority fee and bribe together.

dials.label: Priority fee
dials.help: Used with Manual, and by Auto when live fee data is missing.

dials.label: Bribe
dials.help: Used with Manual, and by Auto when live fee data is missing.

dials.label: Starting balance
dials.help: Used the next time the account is reset.
